comment: Honestly $1 more a month for Premium is still a steal when you factor in no ads, downloads and Connect. My collaborative playlists with friends are the reason I'm not leaving, Tidal sounds better but I'd have to rebuild everything. Worth it for me, I'd pay even more.

Spotify is still absurdly cheap for the catalog, I'll grant them that. But they're raising prices while artists get almost nothing per stream, so I want to see some of this go to the people who make the music. I'll pay, but the pay split needs to change too.

Price doesn't really bother me, I'm more focused on whether they keep the features I actually use. Spotlight still works for me and that's what keeps me around. Hope they don't pull more stuff without warning.

I'm still on free so this doesn't hit me directly, but $11 for Premium is a lot when free only gets shuffle. Ads every few songs is what keeps me questioning whether Premium is worth it at all. Probably sticking with the free tier.

Student plan going from $4.99 to $5.99 isn't great, but it's still a good deal with Hulu included. The bigger issue for me is that Showtime was already dropped with nothing replacing it. I'm staying on student, it's dumb not to use it.

Premium going up a dollar is annoying but it's not the main issue. What really gets me is the UI changes burying library stuff and podcasts getting shoved everywhere. YouTube Music is a great deal and I keep thinking about switching.
The price hike is whatever, I'm more annoyed that I still don't have a true random shuffle. Paying more for something that keeps replaying the same top songs is a joke. Fix shuffle first.

Premium is still the best value of anything I pay for. Ad-free, unlimited skips, downloads, casting, I'm not going back to free for any amount of money. A buck more a month is fine by me, the free tier is just too restricted.

A price increase on top of bugs that still aren't fixed is a hard sell. I've already rolled back versions and reinstalled and the downloads still break. Hope support actually fixes things before they start charging more.

Premium is the one subscription I never cancel, so an extra dollar doesn't change that for me. The trial confusion and renewal prompts are way more annoying than the price. Still worth it for the no ads.

Premium is worth every penny and a dollar more doesn't change that. No ads, offline, unlimited skips, I use it every day. The price is still reasonable for what you get, my only gripe is how free users get treated.

The price doesn't bug me, the home screen does. It looks like TikTok with huge blocks of suggestions and I'm done if they don't revert it. I'll cancel my membership and go to Tidal or Apple Music if this layout stays.

I already cancelled Premium over the feature changes so the price bump isn't really relevant to me. I still use Spotify for the playlists and my workarounds, but the enhance feature keeps mixing recommended songs into my own playlists. Artists paying to get onto playlists is pretty gross too.

Spotify is still at 320kbps while Tidal and Apple give lossless for similar or cheaper money. Paying more with no lossless is hard to justify, even if 320 is fine on AirPods. They need to say when lossless is coming.

Price is fine, I don't mind paying for Spotify since the library is huge. My main complaint is still the repetitive recommendations and the new UI hiding Discover Weekly. I'll keep using it, the algorithm still beats Apple Music in my book.
Another price bump, sure, but my real problem is the liked-song hearts that vanished. I'd unsubscribe again if they don't bring them back. Apple Music is still on the table.

Paying for Premium and still getting podcast ads is the real insult, the price bump just adds salt. Spotify keeps shoving podcasts onto my home screen and I can't hide them. Gotta make money somehow I guess, but this is annoying.

Still worth every penny for me, I use it every day in the car and the skips and offline stuff are great. A buck isn't the end of the world. My issue is ads getting heavier over time and perks disappearing.

Nickel and dime, that is what this is. They removed the heart button and now want more money for features that used to come standard. I'll keep using playlists until they lock more stuff behind a paywall.
The price hike doesn't matter much to me, but a home screen full of podcasts is driving me nuts. I can't find my music and the app is laggy. If the layout stays like this I'll be looking at Deezer.

I already canceled Premium over the redesign and a price increase doesn't help. The music tab is still a dumb card layout instead of album tiles. I'd switch to Apple Music if they don't fix it, my trial is almost up anyway.

The price increase is fine if it comes with lossless, but Spotify still doesn't have it. Apple Music's lossless and Spatial Audio make Spotify look behind. I'm still using it for Connect and Android Auto, but I'm watching this closely.

The price rise doesn't matter to me, what matters is that artists get fractions of a cent per stream. I already moved to Apple Music over that and I'm not coming back until the royalty structure changes. Spotify is cheap for listeners and that's the problem.

The family plan still works out pretty cheap per person and is worth it for us. The price bump is fine as long as the plan doesn't get messed up or we get forced onto a duo. Logistics are what I care about.

Spotify wanting to charge more while still not offering lossless is what bugs me. Tidal and Qobuz do lossless for similar money, and I still have to keep two services. I'll keep Spotify for Connect but this raises the pressure.
Price isn't my thing, I just want the old layout back so I can listen. I rolled back and disabled auto-updates to keep the old version. I'll cancel the day they force the new layout on me.

I already cancelled, and the renewal pop-up keeps showing up every time I open the app. The price hike doesn't matter when the pop-up is in the way of pausing and skipping. I cleared the cache and reinstalled and nothing worked.

Price isn't really the thing for me, I care about the features and they keep removing stuff like album radio and hiding playcounts. It's still the most feature-rich option, so I'll stick around unless more gets cut.
